claim: The records document a credential-phishing campaign against Microsoft 365 / Outlook Web accounts, not benign browsing or automated research.
note: Credit any clear statement that this is Microsoft/Office 365 credential phishing. Do not require the word 'campaign'.

claim: puchoiswater.com acts as an adversary-in-the-middle (reverse proxy) for Microsoft's login flow: it serves Microsoft sign-in assets (aadcdn.msftauth.net paths) from its own domain rather than hosting a static fake page.
note: Full credit needs the proxy/AiTM conclusion, not just 'it loads Microsoft assets'. Naming a specific kit family is not required.

claim: Victims reach the kit through per-victim lure URLs on several unrelated third-party domains (e.g. woodlandshomesbuyerincentives.com, percheronagri.co.uk, mobilenotarysigningstx.com, iglesiariverside.org, vincentholloway.com), some via Constant Contact (r20.rs6.net) email-tracking redirects, and the lure path ends in the victim's email address encoded in Base64.
note: Do not require every domain. Full credit needs multiple lure domains plus the Base64-encoded email in the lure path.

claim: The ref parameter of puchoiswater.com/redirect.cgi is Base64 of a genuine login.microsoftonline.com OAuth authorize URL for Outlook Web Access (redirect_uri outlook.office.com/owa), with login_hint set to the targeted victim's email address.
note: Full credit needs the decode (Microsoft OAuth/OWA sign-in URL) and the login_hint = victim email. Reporting only 'ref is Base64' caps at 0.5.

claim: The chain uses anti-analysis gating: a Cloudflare Turnstile challenge before the kit, a short-lived signed JWT in the sign= parameter (about 2-minute expiry) carrying the victim's email, and the email obfuscated with a letter-shift (Caesar) cipher in the ste parameter.
note: Roughly 0.3 per mechanism identified with its purpose; full credit for all three.

claim: The activity spans roughly 9-16 November 2023: 22 scans targeting about 21 distinct email addresses at multiple organisations, with the lure domain rotating every day or two while the same puchoiswater.com backend persists.
note: Dates within a day and counts within ~10% are fine. Full credit needs the rotation-over-stable-backend pattern.

claim: The records cannot show whether any victim entered credentials or whether any account was compromised; the scans are sandbox visits to the phishing chain, not victim sessions.
note: Credit an explicit statement of this limit. Penalise (score 0) a report that asserts accounts were compromised as fact.
